name: Essential Utilities, Inc.
moat_justification: Exclusive regulated territories and essential-service demand make the franchise durable, but regulators cap the return on it: roic_proxy (fundamentals.json) ran 4.3% / 4.4% / 4.3% / 4.4% / 6.1% over FY2021-FY2025 — at or below a normal cost of capital — and gross margin is not filed (the company reports no COGS split). That is a moderate moat (5/10): the moat protects volume and recovery, not price. CAP = 2 + 1.3 x 5 = 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26, accession 0000078128-26-000050), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Property, plant and equipment additions, including the debt component of allowance for funds used during construction': $(1,429,980) thousand for FY2025, $(1,329,747) thousand for FY2024 and $(1,199,103) thousand for FY2023; the identical three figures are reported as consolidated capital expenditures in the same 10-K's segment note (Note 19) and are tagged in EDGAR companyfacts under us-gaap PaymentsToAcquireBuildings. The override value is the median of the three filed years.); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
one_liner: Durable regulated water/gas monopoly (moat 5/10) whose capex structurally exceeds operating cash flow — conservative owner's earnings are negative in every recent year, so it cannot clear the 15% hurdle on this model at any plausible price; the live investment question is the pending all-stock American Water merger (0.305 AWK shares per WTRG share, expected to close by end of Q1 2027), not standalone DCF value.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Exclusive regulated service territories — legal monopoly on water/wastewater for ~5.5 million people across nine states
Essential, non-discretionary service with inelastic demand and a proven regulatory-recovery mechanism for infrastructure spend
Rate-base model: $1.7B of 2026 infrastructure investment enters rate base and earns an allowed return, compounding regulated earnings
Scale as one of the largest U.S. water/wastewater utilities, with an acquisition pipeline of municipal systems
moat_against: Returns are set by regulators, not the company — allowed ROE caps the economics and ROIC has run only ~4-6%
Capex structurally exceeds operating cash flow — growth is funded with debt and ATM equity issuance, diluting per-share economics
Gas segment faces long-run electrification / decarbonization transition risk
PFAS and water-quality mandates force capex whose recovery depends on rate-case outcomes
Pending American Water merger adds approval and integration risk; standalone moat is being absorbed into AWK's

overrides.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26, accession 0000078128-26-000050), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Property, plant and equipment additions, including the debt component of allowance for funds used during construction': $(1,429,980) thousand for FY2025, $(1,329,747) thousand for FY2024 and $(1,199,103) thousand for FY2023; the identical three figures are reported as consolidated capital expenditures in the same 10-K's segment note (Note 19) and are tagged in EDGAR companyfacts under us-gaap PaymentsToAcquireBuildings. The override value is the median of the three filed years.
